Director. Molecular Genetics.

Hyperhomocysteinemia is a risk factor for arterial
disease and venous thrombosis. Homocystelne levels
are affected by nutritional and genetic factors.
Since NTHFR is involved in methyiation of
homocysteine to methionine, individuals with
MTHFR gene mutations that reduce enzyme activity
may develop hyperhoncystelnemia and thus be at risk
for vascular disease.
The C677T and A1298C mutations are detected by
signal amplification of the MTHFR gene by allelespecific hybridizations and cheniluninescent
detection of hybridized probes. Since genetic
variation and other factors can affect the accuracy
of direct mutation testing, these results should be
interpreted in light of clinical and familial data.
